text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
LES ECHOS
-- Government likely to present mini-budget in autumn and will not implement further cuts in the number of civil servants.
-- European Union partners at Amsterdam reach difficult compromises on a reform of Europe.
-- Investigators into bankruptcy of Comipar and Pallas Stern bank seek up to eight billion francs in damages from auditing firms which approved the accounts.
LA TRIBUNE
-- European partners struggle to reach deal on a reform of Europe.
-- Finance and Industry Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn prepares opinion for a possible delay in some social measures if public deficit overshoot targets.

-- Businessman Francois Pinault starts legal action against the CDR state holding company set up to sell off Credit Lyonnais assets, to block CDR from selling its 24.5 percent stake in Artemis holding to another state holding company.
-- Thomson-CSF and Siemens create joint-venture in air traffic control.
-- LVMH buys a 0.23 percent stake in Grand Metropolitan.
-- Bank of France governor Jean-Claude Trichet criticises distortions of competition in the French banking sector, notably low interest rates on loans.
L'AGEFI

-- Prime Minister Lionel Jospin to deliver keynote policy speech to parliament tomorrow; some of his electoral pledges are already seen as difficult to live up to after the signing of the EU "stability pact" in Amsterdam.
LE FIGARO-ECONOMIE
-- LVMH buys shares in Grand Metropolitan to try and block its planned merger with Guinness in which LVMH holds a 14.2 percent stake.
-- Government considers postponing presentation of a mini-budget until September.
LIBERATION (Economic section)
-- Report by national audit agency Cour des Comptes points to overspending in arms programmes, lack of transparency of military budgets.
THE INTERNATIONAL HERALD TRIBUNE
-- Europe Union leaders clash over defense and power-sharing issues, casting doubt on their ability to reach a consensus on reform.
